problem.name: Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant
problem.statement_latex: Given a 3-manifold by a genus-$g$ Heegaard splitting and mapping-class word $x$, estimate its normalized Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant, represented as the matrix element $\langle v|\rho(x)|v\rangle$ after the standard $\mathcal D^{g-1}$ prefactor. The level is fixed and admissible.
problem.statement_text: Given a 3-manifold by a genus-$g$ Heegaard splitting and mapping-class word $x$, estimate its normalized Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant, represented as the matrix element $\langle v|\rho(x)|v\rangle$ after the standard $\mathcal D^{g-1}$ prefactor. The level is fixed and admissible.

quantum.headline_latex: Polynomial time in the word length, genus and $1/\varepsilon$ by Garnerone--Marzuoli--Rasetti's quantum recoupling algorithm.
quantum.headline_text: Polynomial time in the word length, genus and $1/\varepsilon$ by Garnerone–Marzuoli–Rasetti's quantum recoupling algorithm.

classical.headline_latex: Classical propagation through the full conformal-block basis is exponential in genus for fixed nontrivial level; contraction methods exploit smaller presentation width when available. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
